leads.name: Bodhi/Peepul Tree
leads.reason: Girth 9.1m, height 70ft, vitality Excellent per register; a Ficus religiosa on Big Island soil is a strong candidate. Blocked for now under hard rule 10's school-grounds test: could not find evidence this pass that the former Riverside Elementary School grounds are genuinely open to the public (it appears tied to the historic Riverside/Hilo High School site along the Wailuku River; a 'Riverside Park' name surfaces in passing but was not confirmed as the same open ground). Needs a source stating the grounds are open (a public path, weekend access, or similar) before it can ship.

leads.name: 'Ohi'a Lehua
leads.reason: Register vitality Fair, no girth. Sources describe ohia lehua only as generic surrounding vegetation at Rainbow Falls, never naming an individual specimen the way the banyan there is named ('the ancient banyan tree' at the upper viewing area). Could not find a second source treating this as one identifiable, collectible tree rather than part of the tree cover. Worth another pass with iNaturalist geotagged observations right at the falls viewing platform, or a call to the park.

leads.name: Weeping Fig

leads.name: Monkeypod

leads.name: Coconut
leads.reason: No girth/height. Not researched; coconut palms are common island-wide and this specimen would need a specific story (age, planting history) to clear the collectible-point bar rather than reading as an ordinary palm.

leads.name: Gold Tree
leads.reason: Not researched this pass. The Hilo Forestry (Ho'olulu) Arboretum is a genuine public site and worth checking; a flowering gold tree is visually striking when in bloom.
